key_results: Individual oligodendrocyte processes extend past axon branch points before ensheathment, forming chains of myelin sheaths connected by paranodal bridges; flexible ensheathment enables single process to myelinate highly branched parvalbumin interneuron axons; terminal sheaths degenerate more frequently in aged brain
comments: Novel mechanism explaining how oligodendrocytes achieve efficient coverage of complex branched circuits; aging vulnerability of terminal sheaths suggests potential therapeutic target for myelin maintenance.

model_io.model: Zebrafish and mouse CNS with two-photon imaging of myelination

hypotheses.hypothesis: Individual oligodendrocyte processes form single continuous myelin sheath per axon
hypotheses.result: Rejected; processes extend past branch points forming chains of sheaths connected by cytoplasmic bridges

hypotheses.hypothesis: Flexible ensheathment enables efficient myelination of branched axons in complex circuits
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; paranodal bridges allow single process to cover highly branched parvalbumin interneuron axons
